basis.title: Calculation basis
income: 2026 year-end tax settlement for earned income (Income Tax Act §47, §55, §59)
Earned income deduction → basic deduction (self + dependents × 1.5M KRW) and social insurance → 6–45% rates → earned income tax credit
Applies the better of a 15% credit on medical (above 3% of gross salary) and education expenses or the 130K KRW standard tax credit
capitalGains: Home sale under the 2026 Income Tax Act (assumes a sale today in a non-regulated area)
One home per household held 2+ years is exempt; only the sale price above 1.2B KRW is taxed · long-term holding deduction · 2.5M KRW basic deduction
Rates 6–45% (60–70% if held under 2 years). For regulated-area surcharges or temporary two-home cases, use the Capital Gains Tax Calculator

tax.title: Tax Calculator

whatIs.title: What is the Tax Calculator?
whatIs.description: An all-in-one Korean tax calculator for income tax, VAT, and capital gains tax. It applies NTS rates and basic deductions so you can see your tax and after-tax amount at a glance.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Select the type of tax: income tax, VAT, or capital gains tax.
2. Enter your income amount and applicable deductions.
3. Results update as you type, with a line-by-line breakdown and a composition chart.
4. Share a link to the result or save it to your calculation history.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Income tax uses progressive rates (6%–45%), so make full use of income deductions such as personal exemptions and tax credits such as pension savings and medical expenses.
Contributing ₩6M to pension savings and ₩3M to IRP yields up to ₩1.485M in tax credits (16.5% incl. local tax for total salary ≤ ₩55M).
Business owners should manage tax invoices carefully to utilize input VAT credits.
A single-household owner who holds a home for 2+ years (plus 2 years of residence if it was in an adjusted area when acquired) pays no capital gains tax on a sale price up to ₩1.2B.
For complex tax situations, consult a certified tax accountant for legal optimization.

items.q: How are income tax rates determined?
items.a: Korea uses progressive rates from 6% to 45%: under ₩14M at 6%, ₩14M–50M at 15%, ₩50M–88M at 24%, above ₩88M from 35% to 45%.

Individual businesses with prior-year sales (incl. VAT) under ₩104M are simplified taxpayers (sales × industry value-added rate 15–40% × 10%, i.e. 1.5–4% of sales); others are general taxpayers (10%). Simplified taxpayers with annual sales under ₩48M are exempt from payment, but input VAT credit is limited to 0.5% of purchases.

A single-household owner who has held a home for 2+ years qualifies for exemption; if the home was in an adjusted area when acquired, 2+ years of residence is also required. Luxury homes (sale price over ₩1.2B) are taxed on the excess.

items.q: Do I need to file local income tax separately?
items.a: Local income tax is 10% of income tax. Employers withhold it through payroll and year-end settlement, but if you file a comprehensive income tax return you must also file and pay local income tax to the local government. After filing on Hometax you can continue to Wetax to file and pay it.
